A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original uncertainty-estimation experiments, downstream task evaluations, and ablations in Sections 4.1-4.5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds scene-wise regularization results and a controlled perturbation study in Appendices C and G.

M1.justification: The frozen Gaussian representation, spherical-harmonic uncertainty channels, residual least-squares objective, Bayesian-inspired regularization, and downstream uncertainty-guidance procedures are retained. Added explanations and settings disclosures do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: V2 Appendix G adds Gaussian-blur and Gaussian-noise training conditions on the existing Mip-NeRF360 bicycle scene. This extends input-condition coverage, while the benchmark datasets and downstream tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1-7 retain their comparator sets, including Manifold† in active view selection and the existing scene-change and anomaly-detection baselines. The new scene-wise plots retain FisherRF, and the perturbation study introduces no competing method.

E3.justification: Appendix G introduces a controlled evaluation with 5%/10% corrupted training views and 64/16/4-view reconstructions. It measures relative mean test-view uncertainty against uncorrupted, full-view training. The previously reported benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds a focused study testing whether predicted uncertainty responds to image corruption and reduced training-view counts. Appendix C also extends the existing regularization sensitivity analysis with scene-wise curves and exceptions. Earlier ablations and qualitative analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for its experimental comparisons. The new results retain point-estimate reporting; predicted uncertainty itself is not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1-7 retain their numerical values. V2 adds scene-wise curves revealing FisherRF's lower L1 AUSE on treehill, plus perturbation results in Table 8, including reported uncertainty increases of 122%, 266%, and 596% for 64, 16, and 4 training views. These are additional results, not improved scores under the original benchmark settings.

T1.justification: Equations 1-13, the least-squares and regularization formulations, and Appendix A's derivation preserving linearity with spherical harmonics are unchanged. V2 adds no substantive mathematical result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: post-hoc view-dependent uncertainty estimation, preserved rendering fidelity, dense/sparse capture applicability, and improvements on the same three downstream tasks. The conclusion preserves this scope.

C2.justification: Sections 3.2 and 5 newly explain that the prediction combines aleatoric, epistemic, and optimization-related effects without disentanglement or a probabilistic distribution. V2 also discusses limited regularization benefits in dense capture and scene-specific exceptions. The earlier coarse-primitive resolution limitation is retained.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a promised future code release with an advertised code/project link. V2 newly specifies zero regularization for the dense-view results and midpoint thresholding for change masks, and adds memory-footprint discussion. These are documentation additions rather than evidence that existing experiments changed.

R1.justification: V2 refines the introduction's parameter-space versus rendered-pixel positioning and adds a comparison of disentanglement and probabilistic outputs with prior methods in Section 5. The same 64 works remain cited; publication-status and bibliographic updates do not constitute new related works.

P1.justification: V2 tightens several paragraphs, shortens metric explanations and the conclusion, and changes the running name to 3DGS-Uncertainty. Limitations move into the main text, references precede the appendix, and appendix sections are reorganized. The principal narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds scene-wise plots in Figures 8-10 and the perturbation Table 8 and Figure 13. Existing displays largely retain their designs, with relocations and caption refinements. V1's qualitative Figures 8-9 survive as v2's Figures 11-12.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens supporting evidence through scene-wise analysis and controlled perturbations, while making the uncertainty proxy's limitations and experimental settings clearer. These provide a modest gain in transparency and validation. Main benchmark results remain unchanged, and the new perturbation study is limited to one scene with unspecified corruption strengths.
